title: Timbalamhala
summary: The timbalamhala is a court ensemble of tuned trumpets made from sable and impala antelope horns, played with large and small drums. Each musician blows a single horn of a different pitch, so the tune is passed from horn to horn, and the players are also the dancers.
howToPlay: Each horn is a lane: strike the horn that is due to sound.
The horn lights, a band of breath runs along it and rings of sound leave its opening.
The longer horns sound lower, the shorter ones higher.
rules: A call is a line of long notes, each struck close to its beat.
Long notes swell slowly: strike on the beat and let them ring.
The round ends when the last note has been judged; the score is the share of the best possible.
heritageNote: The players march behind each other in a circle that widens and narrows with the drum beat, and rival ensembles from different sub-chiefs compete before judges.
credits: Tradition: the timbalamhala; figures written for this game
